case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

## Recommendation
- Go to the **Grand Haven pier**. I'd expect pier fishing there to be about **1 of 4** (below average).
- St. Joseph is close behind at about **1 of 4**. Muskegon and South Haven look weaker, at about **0 to 1**.
- Don't count on the pier this week. Boats have been doing better, so if you can get out, boat fishing is the better bet.

## Why
- The Aug 13 Grand Haven report said pier action "had slowed down significantly for salmon due to the warmer water temperatures," so I'd expect the pier to stay slow while the water is this warm.
- The Aug 6 Grand Haven pier anglers still caught a few salmon on alewife and glow spoons, the best pier result from either recent week, so Grand Haven has the strongest recent pier signal.
- Both Muskegon pier reports (Aug 6 and Aug 13) were slow, so I'd expect Muskegon to be the weakest of the four.
- South Haven has no pier report in the last six weeks, so its rating is a guess based on its slow boat report.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (newest is Aug 13, six days old)**
- Grand Haven, Aug 13: pier quality 0 (slow); boats quality 3 (good) at 60–110 ft down in 100–180 ft of water, on green or yellow meat rigs and glow spoons.
- Grand Haven, Aug 6: pier quality 1 (below average), "a few salmon on alewife or while casting glow spoons"; boats quality 1 (below average).
- Muskegon, Aug 13: pier quality 0 ("unsuccessful"); boats quality 2 at 60–100 ft down.
- Muskegon, Aug 6: pier quality 0 with spoons; boats quality 2 at 50–120 ft.
- South Haven, Aug 13: boats quality 0, "a tough week," best water about 120 ft. No pier data.
- St. Joseph, Aug 6: pier quality 1, shrimp, "steelhead and the occasional Chinook." Aug 13 was quality 0 (slow), with no method given.

**Past seasons (history, not current)**
- Matching weeks with surface water near 76 F (within 3 F) had no pier reports. The matches were mostly boat reports, and they were mixed, from slow to excellent.
- Those past boat reports suggest that deeper water (about 90–120 ft) was often where the fish were.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water (measured): St. Joseph (45026) 77 F, South Haven (45168) 76 F, Grand Haven and Muskegon (45161) 75 F. Each was down about 2 F over the week.
- A 2 F drop is not a sharp upwelling signal. Upwelling is what brings salmon to the piers (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension, general guidance).
- I don't have a modeled pierhead temperature or a wind forecast for these ports, so I can't check for a pier-level upwelling.

## Caveats
- The newest reports are from Aug 13, six days old. Pier conditions can change quickly, so check the next DNR report before you go.
- Current conditions returned a backtest summary for the week before Aug 19, not live data. Those buoy numbers are measured, but they're not today's readings.
- Grand Haven vs. St. Joseph is a close call. Both had one slow-to-below-average pier report, and neither has a recent pier report that was good.
- South Haven's rating rests on a boat report and no pier data.

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph bulletin, Aug 13, 2025: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3edac95
- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph bulletin, Aug 6, 2025: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3ecb2c3
